hints: Focus on what type of hydrolysis this is, alkaline with NaOH does not give a carboxylic acid.
Write the equation for propyl ethanoate + NaOH and identify the two carbon-containing products, propan-1-ol and sodium ethanoate.
Calculate $M_r$ of each organic product and express each as a percentage of their combined mass.
walkthrough:
**Identify the alkaline hydrolysis products**

Alkaline hydrolysis of an ester gives a carboxylate salt plus an alcohol, not a carboxylic acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Calculate the $M_r$ of each organic product**

Both products contain carbon, so both count as the organic products to be weighed.

$$M_r(\text{propan-1-ol, C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}) = 36 + 8 + 16 = 60$$
$$M_r(\text{sodium ethanoate, C}_2\text{H}_3\text{O}_2\text{Na}) = 24 + 3 + 32 + 23 = 82$$

**Find percentage by mass of the mixture**

One mole of ester gives one mole of each product, so total product mass per mole is $60 + 82 = 142$.

$$\% \text{propanol} = \frac{60}{142} \times 100 = 42.3\%$$
$$\% \text{sodium ethanoate} = \frac{82}{142} \times 100 = 57.7\%$$

options.A: Incorrect. This swaps the acid and alcohol parts of the ester. It is the answer if you think the products are ethanol ($M_r = 46$) and sodium propanoate ($M_r = 96$), giving 46/142 and 96/142. But propyl ethanoate is ethanoic acid + propanol, not propanoic acid + ethanol.
options.B: Incorrect. This is close to the result if KOH were used instead of NaOH. Potassium ethanoate ($M_r \approx 98$) with propanol ($M_r = 60$) gives about 38% and 62%. The question clearly states aqueous NaOH, so use $Na = 23$, not $K$.
options.C: Correct. Alkaline hydrolysis gives propan-1-ol ($M_r = 60$) and sodium ethanoate ($M_r = 82$). Total = 142, so percentages are 60/142 x 100 = 42.3% and 82/142 x 100 = 57.7%.
options.D: Incorrect. This is the trap for acid hydrolysis. With dilute acid you would get ethanoic acid ($M_r = 60$) and propanol ($M_r = 60$), which would indeed be 50.0% each. With NaOH you get the sodium salt ($M_r = 82$), so the masses are unequal.
